key_insight: Layered compliant coatings can alter near-wall turbulent responses, with fluid-facing material setting interfacial wave speed and subsurface stiffness modifying effective panel thickness.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports screening passive coating designs for potential skin-friction reduction before costly high-fidelity simulations and experiments.
method: Couple linearized fluid resolvent dynamics to a Galerkin model of layered viscoelastic solids.
Condense solid dynamics into a spectral surface-impedance operator.
Assess temporal stability and estimate drag changes using leading-order response covariances.
evidence_signal: At Reτ = 180, stiff panels approach rigid-wall behavior while more compliant panels modify the near-wall low-rank response; additional studies examine Reynolds-number scaling, damping, and layering.
watch_item: Predicted drag changes are leading-order estimates, and unstable parameter regimes limit the relevance of steady harmonic responses.
paper_title: Resolvent-based modeling of turbulent flow over multilayer compliant surfaces
